what: Independent third check of the steering additions at 8f054953 (the heat average started from the margin, the averages comparison, the weight table, the documents): two reviewers (code; measurement and documents), each followed by a skeptic who re-checked every finding.

findings.title: Docs overstate how well the warm-started average follows F2 near and under the margin ('0.80-0.82 of F2's price', 'below the margin it adds nothing', 'a cool drive starts at the margin and falls below it')
findings.location: hardware/triceratops_build/rl/README.md, 'The steering run's training additions' (heat bullets: 'over 2-20 s the cost comes to 0.80-0.82 of F2's own price ... walking or with action noise' and 'below the margin it adds nothing'); trike_env.py w_heat_peak comment (lines 171-184: 'a cool drive starts at the margin and falls below it', 'about 0.8 of F2's own price'); DECISION_LOG D29 and PLAN_STEERING_RUN.md status ('prices 0.80-0.82 of F2's own price')
findings.evidence:
I reproduced heat_average_comparison.md byte for byte and kept the per-step logs (72 episodes). The 0.80-0.82 share holds only for groups well over the margin. The walking group at 0.15 m/s (deterministic) is 1.26 in the committed table. Per episode with 'warm':
- F2 0.803 costs 0.0256/step against F2's 0.0023 (11x).
- F2 0.805 costs 0.0145 against 0.0048.
- F2 0.825 costs 0.0271 against 0.0228.

All 8 episodes with F2 under 0.8 (0.72-0.78) pay 0.0006-0.0156 per step, and their last charged step is at 4.5-20 s (16.2 s and 20 s in two of them). On A1's own example (fore128-s0, seed 100001, 0.15 m/s, F2 0.729) the env, which I checked equals the offline 'warm' exactly, charges 0.0047/step, peaks at 0.087 in 2-3 s, and puts 98 % of that small cost in 2-4 s (bc: 0.029/step, peak 0.795).

The cause is the ripple of a 4 s average on a ~1.5 s stride, plus the max over 12 drives and local 4 s hot spells. That is inherent to tau 4 s, not caused by the warm start. A synthetic square wave at RMS 0.78-0.79 is still charged on 26-39 % of steps after 8 s. The README's later bullet does say '1.26 on the lowest group' and '0.005 per step on gaits under the margin', so this is a matter of wording.
findings.suggested_fix: Qualify the claims. 0.80-0.82 of F2's price applies to gaits well over the margin. Near or under it, the stride ripple of the 4 s average and the max over 12 drives still charge a little: about 0.005 per step on average and up to 0.016, until late in the episode, even when F2 is under 0.8. In the w_heat_peak comment, replace 'falls below it' with 'tends below it'.

findings.title: The new stride-like test's bound sits just above the value it measures, so a harmless 2 % change in the stride period fails it
findings.evidence:
Recomputed with the test's own input. With 'warm', stance first, period 74, cool.max is 0.0497, against a bound of 0.05. Period 76 gives 0.0508 and period 80 gives 0.0532, and both fail; period 90 also fails cool[400:] == 0 (0.0025).

The test does fail on the bias-corrected version. In my scratch mutant M2 (bias correction with the new signature) cool.max is 0.2607 and the hot share 1.21. That discrimination comes only from the stance-first phase: with stance second, bc gives cool.max 0 and a hot share of 0.857, inside 0.7-0.9. The floor-200 variant (M12) passes this test, although tests 1 and 3 catch it.
findings.suggested_fix: Set the bound with headroom, for example 0.06, or state it relative to the bias-corrected price (for example under 0.3 x bc's first-stride peak). Also assert the share of the cost in the first 100 steps, so the test does not rest on one threshold fitted to period 74.

findings.title: D29 says the dev weights 'keep the README's 0.3 margin' at the assumed noise; at 0.15 m/s, weight 0.5 and std 0.175 give +0.28

findings.suggested_fix: In D29, write 'sit at the README's 0.3 margin rule (+0.35 and +0.28 at weight 0.5 and std 0.175; +0.38 at weight 1 and std 0.15)'.

findings.title: The planned re-check 're-run steer_heat_weight.py at that noise' needs a code change, and heavy-robot margins exist only at std 0 and 0.2 and are not in the README

The README says 0.035-0.057. The column now reads "hottest drive's average at 20 s", and margins.md notes that 'hottest drive' is the env's average (tau 4 s) at 20 s. The steer_heat_weight.py docstring lists all three outputs.

On 40 hot episodes, cost per unit of excess is 0.44 in 2-6 s and 0.97 in 10-20 s, so the warm start lowers the early level, not the per-step marginal weight, and gives no incentive to move heat earlier. findings.title: The noise assumption behind weights 0.5 and 1 rests on a false claim: the D22 10 M runs did record action noise all through training
findings.location: hardware/triceratops_build/rl/README.md, 'The weight' bullet ('No 10 M run has a noise figure before its end ... So the assumption is 0.15-0.175 at 3 M'); DECISION_LOG.md D29 ('earlier runs: 0.17-0.18 at 1-2 M'); PLAN_STEERING_RUN.md status; runs/trike60-steer1-dev_STEPS.md section 5
findings.evidence: The D22 runs were trained at commit f84a6919 (run_record git.commit). At that commit train.py (lines 541-544) always attaches TrainingHealth(out / 'train_health.jsonl'), and telemetry/health.py line 146 writes 'action_std' (the mean of exp(log_std)) on every rollout. out is the run's Drive folder (args.out = /content/drive/MyDrive/mesozoic-labs/triceratops60/trike60-fore128-s0). runs/trike60-d22_LOG.md line 41 even cites a D22 train_health.jsonl (213 env steps/s). The D22 runs had the same log_std_init (-1.6), the same 10 M schedule and LR 3e-4 to 3e-5, and the same late ramp (1 M to 3 M) and terrain ramp (1 M to 4 M) as the dev runs (run_record args). So eight 10 M noise trajectories, four of them on the 128 mm model, should be on the owner's Drive. The author reads that Drive. Instead the docs infer the 3 M noise from short runs whose LR annealed to 0 at 1.5-2 M, and from final checkpoints. I reproduced those figures (weights-only loads of log_std): run3_dev probe 0.1775 at 1.0 M, 0.1745 at 1.25 M, 0.172 at 1.5 M; pipe1 0.172 at 2.0 M; fore128-s0..s3 at 10 M 0.0855, 0.0830, 0.0884, 0.0911. The weight choice depends on this number. From the committed table, weight 1 is +0.38 at std 0.15 but +0.20/+0.13 at 0.175, and weight 0.5 is +0.35/+0.28 at 0.175. I could not see the Drive files themselves.
findings.suggested_fix: Before the dev runs, read action_std at 1, 2, 3 and 5 M from the four fore128 train_health.jsonl files. Put the measured range in README, PLAN and D29 in place of 'no 10 M run has a noise figure'. Then re-check whether 0.5 and 1 is still the pair that brackets the 0.3 rule. D22 had no r_heat_peak, so its noise is an upper bound for the dev runs' noise.

findings.title: The margin-started average still loads the start of the window for cool gaits and for drives other than the hottest; 'same weight wherever it falls' and the 1.13 burst ratio are best cases
findings.location: rl/README.md 'every step's heat carries the same weight wherever it falls in the window ... below the margin it adds nothing' and 'a burst at 3 s costs 1.13 times one at 10 s'; trike_env.py w_heat_peak comment; analysis/steer_heat_average.py (the burst test uses the hottest drive of deterministic episodes only)
findings.evidence: From my rerun's logs (scripts a2.py, a4.py, a6.py in scratchpad/check3_steer/scripts). The 8 episodes under the margin pay 39.6 in total under warm. 48 % of that falls in 2-4 s and 66 % in 2-6 s, against 11 % and 22 % of the window's time. The cost rate is 0.024 per step in 2-4 s against 0.0015 in 10-20 s. Including the hinge and the max, the discounted marginal weight on a cool gait's hottest drive is 0.058 at 2.02 s and 0.014-0.019 from 4 s on. On the 2nd-hottest drive (deterministic) it is 0.055 at 2.02 s and 0.012 at 10 s. The 0.5 s burst at 2x rating, with warm: hottest drive 1.13 deterministic but 1.24 at std 0.1 and 1.22 at std 0.2; 2nd-hottest 1.37 deterministic and 1.48 at std 0.2; median drive 5.1 deterministic and 6.0 at std 0.1. bc is worse in every case (2nd-hottest 2.36, median 10.4), so the ranking holds. The magnitudes are an order below bc's (cool gaits 0.0049 against 0.0179 per step).
findings.suggested_fix: Qualify the wording: each drive's mean square weighs every step alike. With the hinge, a cool or non-hottest drive's heat in the first 2-4 s is priced 3-6 times later heat, which is still small. Say the 1.13 is for the hottest drive in deterministic episodes (1.22-1.24 under noise). Optionally add the cool-episode 2-4 s share and a non-hottest-drive burst row to heat_average_comparison.md.

findings.title: '0.80-0.82 of F2's price, a near-constant share' holds for group sums of hot gaits, not near the margin where the deterministic dev policies will sit
findings.location: rl/README.md first heat bullet ('0.80-0.82 ... walking or with action noise'); PLAN status; DECISION_LOG D29; trike_env.py comment ('about 0.8 of F2's own price')
findings.evidence: heat_average_comparison.md gives 1.26 for the 0.15 m/s deterministic group (walking, no noise), so 'walking or with action noise' is true for 5 of 6 groups only. The README states the exception only in the later bullet, and PLAN and D29 omit it. Per episode (a1.py), the warm share is 0.75-0.96 for F2 >= 0.86 but 1.19 at F2 0.825, 3.06 at 0.805 and 11.1 at 0.803. Episodes with F2 0.72-0.78 pay 0.6-15.6 per episode, where F2's price is 0. The square-wave test function gives the same picture: RMS 0.78 and 0.79 inputs cost 0.0066 and 0.0098 per step (stance first). The D22 deterministic hottest drives were 0.83-0.95, so the effective margin of a trained policy is a few hundredths below 0.8 and the weight does not absorb this.
findings.suggested_fix: Write '0.80-0.82 on five of six groups (1.26 on the coolest)'. Add one sentence: near or under the margin the term prices more than F2's hinge (shares of 1.2-11 for F2 0.80-0.83), because the 4 s average ripples with the stride and the cost takes the maximum of 12 drives.

findings.title: The 2-4 s share is presented as favouring the adopted average, but at training noise bc is closer to the time share than warm
findings.location: rl/README.md 'How the average was chosen' ('13-21 % of the cost fell in 2-4 s (11 % of the time)' for bc; '4-5 % of the cost in 2-4 s' for warm)
findings.evidence: From the committed table (reproduced byte for byte), against the 11 % time share: at std 0.2 bc is 0.13 (2 points off) and warm 0.04 (7 points off). At std 0.1 they are 0.16 (5 points off) and 0.04 (7 points off). Only at std 0 is bc further off (0.21 against 0.05). Warm's low share comes from its start below a hot drive's level (it charges heat later), not from equal weighting. The equal-weight case rests on the discounted-weight table (0.33 throughout against 4.43 at 2.02 s) and the cool-gait cost.
findings.suggested_fix: Cite the discounted weights and the cool-gait cost as the reasons for warm. Describe warm's 4-5 % as its start-up deficit on hot drives, the cause of the 0.8 price share, not as a match to the time share.

findings.title: The step sheet's training speeds are run 3's, not the foreleg runs', so the 5 M read comes later than stated for the 128 mm model
findings.location: rl/runs/trike60-steer1-dev_STEPS.md section 1 ('At the foreleg runs' speeds (550-909 steps per second) that is 1.5-2.5 hours in'); PLAN 'Cost and time' ('1.5-2.5 h in')

findings.title: The planned re-check 're-run steer_heat_weight.py at that noise' cannot be done with the script as committed
findings.location: rl/analysis/steer_heat_weight.py (STDS constant, job() loads only fore128-s{i}); README 'Before the judged weight is fixed'; STEPS section 5
findings.evidence: STDS = (0.0, 0.05, 0.1, 0.15, 0.175, 0.2) is hard-coded, and the CLI takes only --runs-dir, --out and --workers. main() builds the run names 'fore128-s0'..'fore128-s3'. findings.title: The sheet and plan give no rule for choosing the judged weight when the two single-seed dev runs differ by less than the 0.1 noise band
findings.location: rl/runs/trike60-steer1-dev_STEPS.md section 5; PLAN 'The runs' ('set the heat cost's weight'); D29
findings.evidence: Section 5 says a hottest-drive difference under about 0.1 'is not read as a weight effect'. The D22 128 mm 5-episode worst drives were 0.828, 0.888, 0.931 and 0.945 (recomputed from analytics/results/fore128-s*/gait_report_episodes.json.gz), so 0.1 is the right size of band. With one seed per weight, the runs can therefore only reject a weight (drift to standing, falls, a failed noise check). The sheet does not say which weight is taken if both pass and the heat differs by less than 0.1. Before 1 M the two runs are the same (r_heat_peak x late scale 0, same seed), so only 1-5 M differs between them.
findings.suggested_fix: Add one line to section 5 or the PLAN: if both runs walk and their hottest drives are within 0.1, take the weight the measured 3 M noise supports under the 0.3 rule (or the higher weight that meets it).

findings.location: DECISION_LOG.md D29; rl/README.md 'The weight'; trike_env.py w_heat_peak comment; tests/test_steer_heat.py docstring; analysis/steer_heat_average.py docstring

verdicts.reasoning:
Most of the evidence holds and I reproduced it. Two of the three quoted phrases do overstate.

1. '0.80-0.82 of F2's own price ... walking or with action noise' (README) and the unqualified 'about 0.8' (trike_env comment), 'prices 0.80-0.82' (D29, PLAN) are true for 5 of the 6 groups. The 6th, 0.15 m/s deterministic, is 1.26, and episodes near or under the margin pay several times their F2 price.

2. 'A cool drive starts at the margin and falls below it' is a simplification. In A1's episode, a drive whose 2-20 s RMS is 0.60 rises from 0.80 to 0.887 by 2.6 s before falling. That drive really is hot early (its 2-4 s RMS is 0.82), so this is a real transient, not an artefact of the warm start.

3. 'Below the margin it adds nothing' is not an overstatement in context. The sentence is about the hottest drive's average ('while the hottest drive's average is over the margin ... below the margin it adds nothing'), so it states the hinge correctly. It is not a claim that gaits whose F2 is under the margin cost nothing.

The README itself already gives '1.26 on the lowest group' and '0.005 per step on gaits under the margin'. So this is wording only; it does not affect the dev runs (the noisy groups that matter are 0.82).
